issues.description: Deprecation decorator wraps a generator function, breaking the context manager protocol
issues.detail: `@contextlib.contextmanager` expects the wrapped callable to be a generator function. Placing `@falcon.util.deprecated` above `@contextlib.contextmanager` means `deprecated` wraps the generator function before contextmanager sees it; if `deprecated` returns a regular function (not a generator), `contextmanager` will fail or behave incorrectly. The decorator order should be reversed, or verified to preserve generator semantics. The test only checks one invocation — confirm it actually yields.
The `.. deprecated:: 4.3` directive says "Use the stlib's :func:`contextlib.redirect_stdout`" — "stlib" should be "stdlib". This text is rendered in user-facing Sphinx docs.

issues.description: Default arguments capture sys.stdout/sys.stderr at import time
issues.detail: Pre-existing in the function, but worth noting since this PR touches it: `stdout: TextIO = sys.stdout` evaluates at definition time, so reassignments to `sys.stdout` (e.g., by pytest's capsys) won't be picked up as defaults. Not introduced by this diff, but the deprecation message could mention this as another reason to prefer stdlib.

issues.description: News fragment classified as `.misc` rather than `.deprecation`
issues.detail: Falcon's towncrier configuration commonly uses a dedicated `deprecation` (or `deprecated`) fragment type for user-visible deprecations. Filing this as `2569.misc.rst` may bury it in the "Misc" section of the changelog instead of a deprecations section. Verify against `pyproject.toml` towncrier types.

issues.description: Test does not assert exactly one warning or warning category specifics
issues.detail: `test_deprecated_redirected` uses `pytest.warns(...)` with a match string but doesn't guard against multiple warnings or assert the warning is emitted on entry vs. exit. Minor, but matches the pattern in `test_deprecated_httpnow` so it's consistent — flagging for awareness only.

review.summary: The PR is small and well-scoped: it adds a deprecation warning to `falcon.testing.redirected`, updates internal call sites to `contextlib.redirect_stdout/stderr`, adds a news fragment, and adds a deprecation test. Main concern is decorator ordering — `@falcon.util.deprecated` is applied above `@contextlib.contextmanager`, which can break the generator-function contract that `contextmanager` requires; this should be verified to ensure `redirected(...)` still works as a context manager and the test exercises actual stdout capture (it does, partially). Minor issues: a "stlib" typo in the deprecation docstring, possible miscategorization of the news fragment as `.misc` instead of a deprecation type, and the pre-existing import-time default-argument capture for sys.stdout/sys.stderr.
